body:
One more spelling in this card's family, from #20234 stage 2 (PR #20342's dev report on #20234). `domain:spec` seat 4 (`session_01CiCTczDo7tGhafXjf61dUJ`).

- `packages/spec/src/api/export-job-family-retirement.test.ts:25` cites 「objectui PR #10264」. `CITATION_RE` recognises only an `owner/repo#` or `repo#` prefix as a qualifier, so this prose spelling is read as a bare number of THIS repository. #10264 answers 404 here, so the gate's census counts a dead in-repo citation that is really objectui's number.
- This is the mirror image of the `pre-` / `post-` case in the body. There, a prefix that is NOT a repository is taken as one. Here, a repository named in prose is not taken as one.
- The suggested fix shape in the body covers both: a closed set of recognised qualifiers, with self-test cases for `pre-#N`, `post-#N` and `objectui PR #N`.

Path: fleet decision — the issue-citation gate judges every spelling it passes | 缺项 (`pre-#N` / `post-#N`) | none

## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `tooling` · `priority:p3` · `domain:spec` · `area:devpath` · `pm:queue`

Triage: lands in `scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs` (`CITATION_RE`'s optional repository prefix, about :328) ⇒ `domain:spec` (the `scripts/` gate anchoring exception). Rationale: `pre-#N` / `post-#N` are read as another repository's reference and never judged. Three of the 18 kernel and contracts sites cited dead numbers, and PR #20326 rewrote those. A strengthening of an existing gate, with no runtime effect ⇒ **p3**.

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01W89enF2dYV7K4N2Fbfj33f` · 2026-09-28T00:24Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. Read: this card (no comments).

**Why it stays open under the maintainer's ruling batch #202 B:** it clears the second reopen reading. The gate protects shipped text (docblocks in `dist`, changesets in the CHANGELOG) from dead citations, under ruling C+D on #19123. A spelling it silently skips is a hole in that contract.

**Execution notes.**
1. A qualifier must be a known repository slug or an `owner/repo` form. `pre-` / `post-` become prose.
2. Add self-test cases for both spellings, including a dead-number case that must go red.
3. Census the other areas for the spelling and record the count. Rewrite any dead one found, the PR #20326 shape.

Two more spellings in this card's family, from #20234 stage 3 (`data/`, PR #20533; dev report `5881236928` on #20234, confirmed by the at-tier record `5881413052`). `domain:spec` seat 2 (`session_014EJ1ED8X4MMrT18BhVx4tx`) · 2026-09-29T00:42Z. ⛔ Not a claim; no label moved.

- **Capitalised qualifiers.** `CITATION_RE`'s qualifier is case-sensitive in effect. `Pre-#N`, `POST-#N` and `Framework#N` are classed as cross-repo and never judged, the same hole as the body's `pre-` / `post-`. `packages/spec/src/data/**` carried 7 sites in these spellings at `9bf5e67af`. One was dead: `object.test.ts:223` `POST-#10347`, which PR #20533 rewrites.
- **A qualifier on the first number of a pair.** In `objectui#6110 + #6111` (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts:370`), the qualifier covers only the first number, so the grammar reads `#6111` as this repository's. It is objectui's live issue: objectui REST answers 200, and there is no `refs/pull/6111/head`. It is the mirror case of seat 4's `objectui PR #10264` note above.

Execution note 1's closed set of recognised qualifiers covers the first spelling if it matches case-insensitively and treats `Pre-` / `POST-` / `Framework` as prose. The pair case needs either a rule for a qualifier carrying across `+` / `and`, or a prose convention of qualifying each number. Self-test cases for both belong with the body's.
